properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 22 at 8:51PM PDT until July 23 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 649 North and Central
Coastal Strip, Fire Weather Zone 650 North Coastal Lowlands,
Fire Weather Zone 651 Central Coastal Lowlands, Fire Weather
Zone 652 West Portion of the Olympic Mountains, Fire Weather
Zone 655 Black Hills and Southwest Interior Lowlands, Fire
Weather Zone 659 West Slopes of the Central Cascades Generally
above 1500 Feet and Fire Weather Zone 661 East Portion of the
Olympic Mountains.

* WINDS...West 5 to 10 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent Thursday.

* LIGHTNING...Isolated thunderstorm coverage is possible across
the southern Cascade Mountains and portions of southwest
Washington. Thunderstorms will develop late Wednesday night
and move from south to north across the area.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Any storms that develop will be capable of
gusty and erratic outflow winds between 25 and 30 miles per
hour. Outflow winds can occur ahead of and behind storms and
cause erratic wind directions.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 85 Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Lightning in dry fuels can cause multiple fire
starts. Thunderstorms can also bring sudden sharp wind shifts
on existing fires, causing rapid changes in a fire's rate of
spread and direction of spread. Thunderstorm outflow winds can
be a threat for several hours following the start of a new
lightning- caused fire. If a fire were to begin, air quality
may diminish in the surrounding area.

* IMPACTS...Scattered lightning in dry fuels can cause multiple
fire starts. Thunderstorms can also bring sudden sharp wind
shifts on existing fires, causing rapid changes in a fire's
rate of spread and direction of spread. Thunderstorm outflow
winds can be a threat for several hours following the start of
a new lightning-caused fire. If a fire were to begin, air
quality may diminish in the surrounding area.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either imminent or occurring now. Any fires that develop will
likely spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

properties.instruction:

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 22 at 10:20PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
HLSLIX

This product covers Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi

TROPICAL STORM BERTHA ABOUT TO MOVE OFF THE SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA COAST
SOUTHWEST OF HOUMA.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Watch has been cancelled for Northern
Hancock, Northern Harrison, Northern Jackson, and St. John The
Baptist

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Jefferson,
Central Plaquemines, Central St. Charles, Coastal Jefferson,
Eastern Orleans, Lower Lafourche, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St.
Bernard, Lower St. Charles, Lower Terrebonne, Southeast St.
Tammany, Southern Hancock, Southern Harrison, Southern Jackson,
Upper Jefferson, Upper Plaquemines, Upper St. Bernard, Upper
St. Charles, and Western Orleans
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Upper Lafourche and
Upper Terrebonne

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 60 miles southwest of New Orleans LA or about 30 miles
west-southwest of Houma LA
- 29.4N 91.1W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 260 degrees at 12 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall near the Biloxi Wildlife
Management Area in St. Bernard Parish, Louisiana at around 200 PM CDT.
The storm is now near the southern Louisiana coast southwest of Houma
and will continue to move westward at a little faster speed.

Coastal flooding has been observed at the Shell Beach and Waveland
observation stations and additional minor to moderate coastal flooding
upwards of 2 to 3 feet is expected during the high tide cycle for
portions of coastal Louisiana and Mississippi through Thursday
morning.

Light rainfall is occurring with this storm over land areas though
additional heavier rainfall will be possible through Thursday for
coastal areas of Mississippi and southeast Louisiana. The threat of
excessive rainfall has decreased across all of southeast Louisiana and
south Mississippi.

No changes have been made to Tropical Storm Warnings with this
advisory package. Tropical Storm Watches have been discontinued for
Lake Maurepas and the inland portions of the Mississippi coastal
counties. No changes to Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories have
been made with this advisory package.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Coastal Southeast Louisiana and Coastal Mississippi. Remain well
sheltered from hazardous wind having possible limited impacts.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Potential limited impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding
across portions of Coastal Southeast Louisiana and Coastal Mississippi.
These  impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
No impacts are anticipated at this time across Southeast Louisiana and
South Mississippi.

* TORNADOES:
No impacts are anticipated at this time across Southeast Louisiana and
South Mississippi.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in New Orleans LA around 5 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

**Tropical Storm Bertha Continues Westward, No Significant Impacts for
Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Watch has been upgraded to a Tropical Storm
Warning for Bolivar Peninsula, Brazoria Islands, Chambers,
Coastal Brazoria, Coastal Galveston, and Galveston Island

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 220 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.4N 91.1W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 260 degrees at 12 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

At 10 PM CDT, Tropical Storm Bertha was located near the southern
Louisiana coast. Bertha will continue to move westward along the
central Gulf Coast tonight and early Thursday. Bertha will be moving
through an unfavorable environment due to high wind shear, dry air, and
land interaction. It is forecast to make another landfall along the
Upper Texas Coast late Thursday morning or early afternoon as a weak
Tropical Storm or Tropical Depression. No significant impacts to
Southeast Texas are expected at this time with the highest
probabilities of tropical storm force winds remaining off the coast and
gusts to tropical storm force winds possible along the immediate
coast. Isolated showers and thunderstorms will be possible through
Thursday, but threat of flooding rain is low. There is also an
increased risk of strong rip currents likely through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across coastal
portions of Chambers, Galveston, and Brazoria counties.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts
across Bolivar Peninsula. Potential impacts in this area
include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across coastal portions of Southeast Texas. Potential
impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

There is a threat from tornadoes with this storm. Have multiple ways
to receive Tornado Warnings. Be ready to shelter quickly.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 4 AM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 22 at 10:03PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropcial Storm Warnings Expanded into Southeast Texas**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Watch has been upgraded to a Tropical Storm
Warning for Lower Jefferson and West Cameron

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Lower
Iberia, Lower Jefferson, Lower St. Mary, Lower Vermilion, and
West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 130 miles east-southeast of Cameron LA or about 20 miles
south-southeast of Morgan City LA
- 29.4N 91.1W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 260 degrees at 12 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Bertha continues to maintain tropcial storm force winds, albiet
mostly over the gulf waters. The storm is moving a bit south of due
west and will move along the coast or just south of southwest
Louisiana through tonight and into southeast Texas late Thursday. Tropical
storm warning have been extended across the remainder of Cameron
Parish and across southern Jefferson County. The warning also now
includes Sabine Lake. The remainder of the forecast remains unchanged
with 1 to 3 feet of surge possible and most of the heavy rainfall
remaining offshore due to the sheared nature of the convection.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
coastal portions of Louisiana and southeast Texas south of I-10.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across immediate coastal portions of Louisiana and southeast
Texas. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across south central and coastal portions of Louisiana
and southeast Texas. Potential impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

If you are relocating to safe shelter, leave as early as possible.
Allow extra time to reach your destination. Many roads and bridges
will be closed once strong winds arrive. Check the latest weather
forecast before departing and drive with caution.

If heading to a community shelter, become familiar with the shelter
rules before arrival, especially if you have special needs or have
pets. Take essential items with you from your Emergency Supplies Kit.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 4 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 22 at 10:54PM EDT until July 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Piedmont and western North Carolina, including
the following areas, in Piedmont North Carolina, Alexander,
Cabarrus, Catawba, Cleveland, Davie, Gaston, Iredell, Lincoln,
Mecklenburg and Rowan. In western North Carolina, Avery, Buncombe,
Burke Mountains, Caldwell Mountains, Eastern McDowell, Eastern
Polk, Graham, Greater Burke, Greater Caldwell, Greater Rutherford,
Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Madison, McDowell Mountains, Mitchell,
Northern Jackson, Polk Mountains, Rutherford Mountains, Southern
Jackson, Swain, Transylvania and Yancey.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations, including
urban areas along the I-77 and I-40 corridors.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Waves of heavy rain showers and scattered thunderstorms are
forecast to move along a slow-moving cold front tonight into
Thursday. While widespread 1-2 inch rainfall amounts are expected
across western North Carolina through tonight, isolated locations
are expected to see multiple rounds of very heavy rainfall, and
localized amounts as high as 5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 22 at 9:53PM CDT until July 26 at 6:15AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Widespread major flooding threatens
livestock over a large area of the flood plain. A mile of Farm to
Market 190 near the river is flooded and flow is within a foot of
the Farm to Market 190 bridge floor over the Nueces River. The
Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a mile and a half wide south and
west of Carrizo Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 29.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 9:30 PM CDT Wednesday was 29.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Saturday evening and continue falling to 15.6 feet Monday
evening.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon by 400 PM CDT.

monitored.

thunderstorms this afternoon, with additional rain still

Roaring Fork Creek, Sweetwater Gap Drain, Tayo Creek, Sheep

deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES THROUGH THURSDAY
NIGHT...

.Forerunners from a moderate, long-period south swell are already
reaching Hawaii this afternoon. The swell builds tonight into
Thursday, with surf increasing to advisory level along south-
facing shores sometime on Thursday. Thursday night into Friday,
the swell may peak near warning level. Long-period south swell
energy will keep surf elevated beyond Friday, which may require
the advisory to be extended through the weekend.

* WHERE...South facing shores of all Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Thursday to 6 AM HST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
properties.instruction:

go out.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 7:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology and the Benton Clean Air
Agency have issued an Air Quality Alert until 9 AM PDT Friday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.


Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 5:41PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley. Levels
of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Monday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 22 at 3:12PM PDT until July 22 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with high temperatures in the 90s to near
100 degrees and low temperatures in the mid 60s. This will pose a
major risk of heat-related illness.

* WHERE...Foothills of the Western and Southern Olympic Peninsula,
Middle Chehalis River Valley, Southern Hood Canal, Foothills and
Valleys of Thurston and Lewis Counties, Lowlands of Lewis and
Southern Thurston Counties, and Olympia and Southern Puget Sound.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Extreme heat will significantly increase the risk of
heat-related illnesses for much of the population, especially
those who are heat sensitive and those without effective cooling
or adequate hydration.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit wa211.org anytime.

properties.areaDesc: Central Brooks Range
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
An Arctic cold front extending from the high arctic will move
southeast towards mainland Alaska. This front will likely bring
chances of precipitation along higher terrain beginning Thursday.
Current model guidance supports the possibility of light rain
Friday morning, with a transition to snow expected towards the
evening and overnight hours. Storm total snowfall accumulations
could be 3 to 5 inches, however with surface temperatures above
freezing, the snow is not anticipated to stick to the road. If the
roads remain wet overnight Friday then there could be patches of
ice, due to air temperatures dipping into the 20s above.

NWSheadline: RAIN/SNOW MIX POSSIBLE IN THE CENTRAL BROOKS RANGE THURSDAY THROUGH FRIDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Wednesday July 22 to 1200 AM Thursday July 23

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Ozone levels are expected to reach the
Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category in the Denver Metro area
on Wednesday. Increased chances of afternoon thunderstorms are
expected to keep ozone in the Good to Moderate range on Thursday.
For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and advisories,
visit: https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx
If possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until midnight, Wednesday
night, July 22, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution
through state policies. For more information about health impacts
and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged

TROPICAL STORM BERTHA HAS MADE LANDFALL IN ST. BERNARD PARISH, LA.
OBSERVED TROPICAL STORM CONDITIONS ARE MOVING INLAND OVER PORTIONS OF
COASTAL SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Jefferson,
Central Plaquemines, Central St. Charles, Coastal Jefferson,
Eastern Orleans, Lower Lafourche, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St.
Bernard, Lower St. Charles, Lower Terrebonne, Southeast St.
Tammany, Southern Hancock, Southern Harrison, Southern Jackson,
Upper Jefferson, Upper Plaquemines, Upper St. Bernard, Upper
St. Charles, and Western Orleans
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Northern Hancock,
Northern Harrison, Northern Jackson, St. John The Baptist,
Upper Lafourche, and Upper Terrebonne

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 30 miles east-southeast of New Orleans LA or about 60
miles southwest of Gulfport MS
- 29.8N 89.8W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 270 degrees at 7 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall near the Biloxi Wildlife
Management Area in St. Bernard Parish, Louisiana at around 200 PM CDT.
The storm continues to move westward and inland into southeast
Louisiana where it will be capable of producing wind gusts upwards of
45 to 50 mph at times within the tropical storm warning and watch
areas, especially near the coastal areas of southeast Louisiana.

Coastal flooding has been observed at the Shell Beach and Waveland
observation stations and additional minor to moderate coastal flooding
upwards of 2 to 3 feet is expected during the high tide cycle for
portions of coastal Louisiana and Mississippi through Thursday
morning.

Light to moderate rainfall is occurring with this storm over land
areas though additional heavier rainfall will be possible through
Thursday for coastal areas of Mississippi and southeast Louisiana. The
threat of excessive rainfall has decreased for areas along and north
of the I-10/12 corridor.

No changes have been made to Tropical Storm Warnings or Watches with
this advisory package. No changes to Coastal Flood Warnings and
Advisories have been changed with this advisory package.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
portions of Coastal Southeast Louisiana and Coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts
across portions of Coastal Southeast Louisiana and Coastal
Mississippi. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible limited
impacts across Coastal Southeast Louisiana and Coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

* TORNADOES:
No impacts are anticipated at this time across Southeast Louisiana and
South Mississippi.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 22 at 2:12PM PDT until July 24 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR THUNDERSTORMS THURSDAY, FIRE WEATHER
WATCHES FOR WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITY FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

A ridge breakdown pattern will first bring an elevated threat for
mountain thunderstorms across portions of central and north-
central Washington tonight into Thursday night. Drier weather
arrives Friday and Saturday, though winds will become increasingly
gusty with critical fire weather conditions likely.

The National Weather Service in Spokane has issued a Red Flag
Warning for abundant lightning, which is in effect from 2 AM
Thursday to 2 AM PDT Friday. A Fire Weather Watch has also been
issued. This Fire Weather Watch for winds and low humidity is in
effect from Friday morning through Saturday evening.

* Affected Area: Okanogan Valley (Zone 703), Methow Valley (Zone
704) and Foothills of Central Washington Cascades (Zone 705).

* Winds: Gusty and erratic outflow winds up to 35mph possible in
any thunderstorms Thursday. West 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to
30 mph Friday, windiest in Okanogan Valley. Saturday, winds 15
to 25 mph with gusts to 40 mph.

* Timing: For the Red Flag Warning, there is an isolated threat
for lightning late tonight into Thursday morning. Scattered
thunderstorms are then expected Thursday afternoon into early
Friday morning. For the Fire Weather Watch, critical wind and
humidity values are expected Friday and Saturday afternoons.

* Relative Humidities: 13 to 21 percent Friday, 14 to 26 percent
Saturday.

* Temperatures: Up to 98 Friday, and up to 94 Saturday.

* Lightning: A 5 to 10% chance of lightning overnight Wednesday
night, with a 30% chance Thursday afternoon into Thursday night.

* Impacts: New fire starts from lightning Thursday. New and
existing fires could be impacted by gusty outflow winds. Gusty
winds and low humidity Saturday afternoon may lead to rapid
fire spread with any new or ongoing fires.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

WATCHES FOR WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITY FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

A ridge breakdown pattern will first bring an elevated threat for
mountain thunderstorms across portions of central and north-
central Washington tonight into Thursday night. Drier weather
arrives Friday and Saturday, though winds will become increasingly
gusty with critical fire weather conditions likely.

The National Weather Service in Spokane has issued a Red Flag
Warning for abundant lightning, which is in effect from 1 PM
Thursday to 2 AM PDT Friday. A Fire Weather Watch has also been
issued. This Fire Weather Watch for winds and low humidity is in
effect from Friday morning through Saturday evening.

* Affected Area: Colville Reservation (Zone 702).

* Winds: Gusty and erratic outflow winds up to 35mph possible in
any thunderstorms Thursday. Southwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up
to 30 mph Friday. Saturday, southwest winds 15 to 20 mph with
gusts up to 35 mph.

* Timing: For the Red Flag Warning, scattered thunderstorms are
then expected Thursday afternoon into early Friday morning. For
the Fire Weather Watch, critical wind and humidity values are
expected Friday and Saturday afternoons.

* Relative Humidities: 15 to 23 percent Friday, 17 to 27 percent
Saturday.

* Temperatures: Up to 98 Friday.

* Lightning: A 5% chance of lightning overnight Wednesday night,
with a 30% chance Thursday afternoon into Thursday night. The
greater chances for lightning will be across the northern
portions of the zone.

* Impacts: New fire starts from lightning Thursday. New and
existing fires could be impacted by gusty outflow winds. Gusty
winds and low humidity Saturday afternoon may lead to rapid fire
spread with any new or ongoing fires.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued July 22 at 4:07PM CDT until July 23 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 6 to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 PM CDT Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM CDT Thursday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Breaking waves can sweep
people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-
threatening swimming conditions and significant beach erosion
can be expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers
away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued July 22 at 2:51PM MDT until July 25 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING ACROSS FAR
SOUTHEAST OREGON ZONES...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop near the Nevada
border and south-central Oregon this afternoon. The thunderstorms
are expected to be a mix of wet and dry. Expect gusty and erratic
winds up to 45 mph in the vicinity of these thunderstorms.

More thunderstorms are expected Thursday afternoon in eastern
Oregon.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for wind and low humidity, which is in effect from Friday
afternoon through Saturday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 401 Western
Payette National Forest, 402 Eastern Payette National Forest
and 423 Owyhee Mountains.

* TIMING...From Friday afternoon through Saturday evening.

* THUNDERSTORMS...None.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

SOUTHEAST OREGON ZONES...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop near the Nevada
border and south-central Oregon this afternoon. The thunderstorms
are expected to be a mix of wet and dry. Expect gusty and erratic
winds up to 45 mph in the vicinity of these thunderstorms.

More thunderstorms are expected Thursday afternoon in eastern
Oregon.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning, which is in effect from noon MDT /11 AM
PDT/ to 9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ Thursday. A Fire Weather Watch has
also been issued. This Fire Weather Watch for wind and low
humidity from Friday afternoon through Saturday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather Zones 673 Central
Canyonlands, 674 Northwestern Vale BLM and 675 Baker Valley.

* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, from noon MDT /11 AM PDT/
to 9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ Thursday. For the Fire Weather Watch,
from Friday afternoon through Saturday evening.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning
tonight and Thursday.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will occur shortly.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 mph.
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Baker, OR; Harney, OR; Malheur, OR
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 2:33PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...High concentration of smoke particulates from wildfires.

* WHERE...Baker, Harney, and Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 1 PM PDT FRIDAY.

* IMPACTS...Smoke can irritate the eyes, lungs and worsen some
medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on
weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:
* Stay inside if possible. Keep windows and doors closed.

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

* Use high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in indoor
ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

* Be aware of smoke in your area and avoid places with the highest
levels.

* If you have heart or lung disease, or asthma, follow your
healthcare provider's advice.

For current Oregon air quality conditions, please visit:
https://aqi.oregon.gov

For additional information, please visit:
https://www.oregon.gov/deq
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Ada, ID; Canyon, ID; Gem, ID; Payette, ID; Washington, ID
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 2:33PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke.

Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy.

* WHERE...Ada, Canyon, Gem, Payette, and Washington Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 2 PM MDT FRIDAY.

* IMPACTS...Everyone may begin to experience health effects; members
of sensitive groups may experience more serious health effects.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's

Boise Regional Office at (208) 373-0550

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 22 at 1:23PM PDT until July 23 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
...The upper level low offshore will shift to the east just
enough today to allow for monsoonal moisture to move into the
region. Instability will accompany the moisture and allow for
increased chances of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across
central Oregon and portions of the eastern mountains. Brief heavy
downpours, gusty outflow winds, small hail, and frequent
lightning will be possible...

The National Weather Service in Pendleton has issued a Red Flag
Warning for abundant lightning, which is in effect from 11 AM to
8 PM PDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 694 Grande Ronde Valley of
Oregon, 695 Eagle Cap Wilderness, 697 Central Blue Mountains
and 699 Western Forested Blue Mountains.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Isolated to scattered dry thunderstorms
Thursday after 1200.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts from 25-45 mph
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Harrison, WV
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 22 at 4:23PM EDT until July 23 at 1:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northeastern Harrison County in northern West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 130 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, and other low-lying is
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 423 PM EDT, The automated gauge on the West Fork River in
Enterprise was reading 16.67 feet and slowly rising. The river is
expected to cross minor flood stage of 17 feet this afternoon and
then drop below minor flood stage this evening. At a stage of 17
feet, flooding of low-lying areas along the river occurs in and
around Enterprise.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Shinnston, Lumberport, Enterprise and Meadowbrook.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 130 AM EDT THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Martin; Pitt; Washington; Tyrrell; Mainland Dare; Greene; Beaufort; Mainland Hyde; Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 22 at 4:04PM EDT until July 24 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following areas, Beaufort, Greene, Mainland Dare, Mainland Hyde,
Martin, Northern Outer Banks, Pitt, Tyrrell and Washington.

* WHEN...From 2 AM EDT Thursday through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A slow moving cold front will approach and then stall over
eastern North Carolina beginning early Thursday morning and
lingering through Friday. Rounds of heavy rainfall and
thunderstorms could bring rainfall totals of 3 to 5 inches.
Heavier amounts will be possible where rainfall rates are the
most intense.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 12:55PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Chelan, Douglas, Garfield,
and Asotin Counties and continues for Spokane, Whitman, Adams,
Ferry, Lincoln, Okanogan, Grant, Adams, Whitman, Pend Oreille, and
Stevens Counties, through Friday, July 24th at 11 AM, due to current
and expected wildfire smoke from regional fires. Particulate matter
(PM2.5) levels are expected to range in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups and Unhealthy categories. In Eastern Okanogan County near
active wildfires, air quality may reach Very Unhealthy to Hazardous
levels. When air quality is Unhealthy, everyone should reduce
exposure. Limit time outside, avoid strenuous activity, and follow
tips for cleaner indoor air.

properties.instruction:
A Heat Advisory means that hot weather conditions are occurring or
expected. This will create a situation in which heat illnesses are
possible.

Never, ever, leave children or pets alone in enclosed vehicles, not
even for a few minutes. Car interiors can reach lethal temperatures
in a matter of minutes.

Stay indoors and seek air-conditioned buildings. Drink water more
than usual, and avoid dehydrating alcoholic, sugary, or caffeinated
drinks. Dress for the heat by wearing lightweight and light colored
clothing. Eat small meals and eat more often. Monitor those with a
higher vulnerability to heat, including small children. Check in on
family, friends, and neighbors, especially the elderly. If engaging
in outdoor activity, take longer and more frequent breaks and avoid
the hottest parts of the day.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

particularly near Lake Creek.

rises. Minor flooding is expected to continue, especially
along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 8:50am the stage was 21.5 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.





- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along Yentna River, stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during

properties.instruction:

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.areaDesc: South Walton; Coastal Bay; Coastal Gulf
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued July 22 at 1:36PM EDT until July 25 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to
8 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...South Walton, Coastal Bay and Coastal Gulf Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT /1 PM
CDT/ this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM
EDT /7 PM CDT/ Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk,
through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...With water levels receding along the
coast and bays, the Coastal Flood Advisory will be allowed to
expire at 1 PM CDT/2 PM EDT.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

stroke.

shelter. Limit time outdoors during the hottest time of the day,
typically from 2 to 7 PM, rest in the shade when possible, and drink
plenty of water. Locate nearby cooling centers through local
resources or dial 2-1-1 in Texas.

properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area on
Thursday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 22 at 6:41AM PDT until July 23 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures up to 103 degrees. This
will pose a moderate to major risk of heat-related illness.

* WHERE...Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon and Washington,
Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon and Washington, Foothills of the
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon, Yakima Valley, and Foothills of
the Blue Mountains of Washington.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Today is expected to be the hottest day, with
Major HeatRisk across the Columbia Basin, Yakima Valley and
portions of the Gorge and Blue Mountain Foothills.

Thursday will also see widespread moderate HeatRisk and locally
major HeatRisk, mainly across the Columbia Basin.

Smoke from area wildfires could end up affecting how hot
temperatures get.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit 211info.org for Oregon or
wa211.org for Washington anytime.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM PDT THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Western Capes
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 5:29AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong Bering Sea system will bring widespread moderate to
heavy rain at times along with gusty winds and rough seas for the
coastal waters of the Kuskokwim Delta and the Western Capes today
and into Thursday.

-Winds: Southerly to southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to
45 mph. Occasional gusts up to 50 mph are also likely. Winds
slowly diminish through Thursday.

-Wave Heights: 5 to 6 ft waves this morning build to 8 to 14 ft
this afternoon. The higher end totals are more likely farther
from the coast. Wave heights slowly subside beginning Thursday
morning.

-Rainfall amounts: Expect moderate to heavy rain at times (about
0.50 to 1.00 inches storm total), with the highest amounts near
Platinum, Quinhagak, and along the Northern Kuskokwim Bay Coast.
Steady rain tapers to showers beginning this afternoon and
evening.

NWSheadline: STRONG WINDS, ROUGH SEAS, AND MODERATE TO HEAVY RAIN ALONG THE KUSKOKWIM DELTA COAST AND WESTERN CAPES TODAY INTO THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 5:29AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong Bering Sea system will bring moderate to heavy rain at
times along the coast as well as gusty winds and rough seas along
the coastal waters of Northern Bristol Bay today and into
Thursday. A southerly push of winds up Nushagak Bay this morning
may bring increased water-levels up the Bay but coastal flooding
is of little to no concern due to lower tides.

-Winds: Southerly winds this morning turn southwesterly through
the day and increasing to 25 to 35 mph with gusts between 35 to
45 mph. Peak winds occur this afternoon into this evening before
slowly diminishing through Thursday morning.

-Wave Heights: Expect peak wave heights of 9 to 13 ft this
afternoon to this evening for the coastal waters of northern
Bristol Bay. The higher end totals are more likely farther from
the coast. Wave heights begin to slowly subside through Thursday
morning.

-Rainfall amounts: Expect a steady light rain with pockets of
moderate rain at times (about 0.50 to 0.75 inches storm total).
The highest rainfall totals will occur near Togiak. Steady rain
tapers to showers through tonight into early Thursday morning.

NWSheadline: STRONG WINDS, ROUGH SEAS, AND MODERATE RAIN ALONG THE NORTHERN BRISTOL BAY COAST TODAY INTO THURSDAY

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 22 at 4:35AM PDT until July 27 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected. Afternoon temperatures
in the desert valleys will climb into the 108 to 114 degree range,
and may exceed 115 along the Colorado River Valley and 120 in Death
Valley. Overnight lows generally 80 to 95 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada including the Greater Mojave Desert region.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ Thursday to 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

SATURDAY EVENING FOR STRONG GUSTY WIND AND LOW RH FOR FIRE
WEATHER ZONES 624 AND 625...

The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Fire Weather
Watch, which is in effect from Friday afternoon through Saturday
evening.

* RED FLAG WARNING AFFECTED AREA...Areas in southern Oregon along
and east of the Cascades, but primarily north and east of a line
from Chiloquin and Sprague River to Lakeview in Fire Weather
Zones 624 and 625.

* THUNDERSTORMS TODAY...Moving roughly north to northeast around
20 mph. Storm mode will be mostly wet thunderstorms, but dry
lightning strikes can occur outside of wet cores. Some of the
stronger storms will contain hail.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Isolated gusts up to 45 mph.

* FIRE WEATHER WATCH AFFECTED AREA...Nearly all areas east of the
Cascades in Fire Weather Zones 624 and 625.

* WINDS...Southwest to west 10 to 20 mph with gusts 30 to 40 mph
both Friday and Saturday afternoon and evening.

* MINIMUM HUMIDITY...5 to 15 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 20 at 7:40PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
have issued an Air Quality Alert until 9 AM PDT Wednesday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.

Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
